findings.description: The adrs list (lines 42-56) omits ADR-SAG-0029 (Active). Its (c) row (docs/architecture.md:1095) governs every serde_json encode/decode failure: INPUT_INVALID with category and line/column only. The delta this sprint owns (decode_failed in payload.rs:104 and its call sites at payload.rs:428 and jev/v1.rs:565) implements that row, and the sprint's own deliverable 9 cites it in substance. The omission is a RULE-ADR-PLAN miss.
findings.remediation: Add `ADR-SAG-0029  # (c) serde_json encode/decode failure: INPUT_INVALID, category and line/column only` to the adrs list in the sprint doc.

findings.description: CheckResponse::into_answers maps a Jev reply to DecisionAnswers, including the answer-type, criteria, probability and range rules, inside sc-decision-schema. The sc-jev caller only delegates (crates/sc-jev/src/check.rs:156). ADR-SAG-0012 r-5 (docs/architecture.md:1035-1039) says sc-jev still implements every Jev HTTP operation, including 'mapping responses'. ADR-SAG-0030 r-5 (docs/architecture.md:1630-1637) sanctions CheckRequest for building and CheckResponse for parsing. It does not name response-to-answer mapping as moving out of sc-jev. Result: violated on the literal text. The ADR-SAG-0012 r-5 subsection is Active, so an amendment is the only path, and it has to be Active before code can stay. Interpretation risk: a reader who treats 'data-only' as covering pure mapping could read this as upheld. The reviewer reads the literal rule.
findings.remediation: Either move the response-to-answer mapping (into_answers, map_answer, check_ranked) into crates/sc-jev and keep CheckResponse as the parsed data type, or land an owner-approved ADR-SAG-0012 r-5 amendment (Active) that names response-to-answer mapping in sc_decision_schema::jev before the code stays. Not fixable inside this review.

findings.description: The binding code sample for CheckResponse::into_answers (in the 'Explicit code samples' block) places response-to-answer mapping in sc_decision_schema::jev::v1. That contradicts ADR-SAG-0012 r-5 (see ARCH-011). RULE-ADR-PLAN treats a plan that contradicts a binding ADR as Blocking even when intended.
findings.remediation: Plan the ADR-SAG-0012 r-5 amendment first (or move the mapping to sc-jev in the plan), then update the sample and the deliverable text to match the Active ADR.

findings.description: ARCH-002 closure is complete for the two named entry points (CanonicalJudgePayload::from_bytes at payload.rs:428 and CheckRequest::parse at jev/v1.rs:565 now use decode_failed, which returns INPUT_INVALID with category and line/column only and a fix hint). Two decode-side sites still use encode_failed: Question::from_json (payload.rs:245) and PayloadBundle::decode (payload.rs:520). Their code is still INPUT_INVALID, which ADR-SAG-0027 and ADR-SAG-0029(c) accept. However, encode_failed's fix hint (crates/sc-agent-types/src/error.rs:833-835) reads '… could not be encoded as JSON' for a parse failure, which is misleading. The stated rule 'encode_failed kept for encode-side sites only' is not what the tree does. Note: the Question::from_json doc block (payload.rs:229-231) says 'EncodeFailed', and the Errors section says INPUT_INVALID.
findings.remediation: Route the two parse-side sites through decode_failed (for example decode_failed("question", &error) at payload.rs:245 and decode_failed("canonical payload", &error) at payload.rs:520), and update the Question::from_json doc. Keep encode_failed for encode-only sites (payload.rs:499, 501, 588; jev/v1.rs:545, 575).

deliverable_checks.notes: Static only. decode_failed emits '{what} is not valid: {category}{at}; fix the {what}' with no body bytes. fix_hint() wraps that detail in 'Correct the input so it matches the expected schema ({detail}), then retry.' Every message the new test checks is produced by this path. Execution of the test was not possible.

Static only. The three cases were traced: an EOF case (CheckRequest::parse), a missing-field case (RawCheckRequest has no defaulted fields, so it is a Data error), and a syntax case (CanonicalJudgePayload::from_bytes). Each yields INPUT_INVALID, contains 'fix the', and omits 'encoded', 'bug' and the secret text. No other test in the repository asserts the old hint wording (grep over crates and docs found none).

Without a diff tool, the annotated line could not be isolated. The pinned toolchain 1.94.1 is confirmed at Cargo.toml:21 and in CI, but that is not the annotation. The two closure-typed annotations in jev.rs (line 169 and line 174) are candidates only. The coordinator or a shell-capable agent must name the exact line from the commit diff.
